subject: Renewal: Quantique Labs – targeted retention & SLA top-up request
messages:
From: Evan Chu <evan.chu@quantique.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@quantique.com>, procurement@quantique.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:32:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal conversation + ask for flexibility

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the partnership over the last two years. Our contract with Redwood is up for renewal on 2027-01-15 (current ARR $285k). We've had a couple of unexpected budget cuts for FY27 and the procurement team is asking for an updated commercial that reduces first-year net cost and adds a stronger SLA for inference latency for our critical endpoints.

Attached is a short note from procurement that outlines their constraints and the program they need to sign off (Quantique_Renewal_Request_2026.pdf). Key asks are: a one-year price reduction (target ~25–30% off list for year one), a one-time service credit (to offset migration work), and an SLA addendum to guarantee p95 latency for our core model route during business hours.

We want to stay with Redwood — product is excellent — but finance is firm about these concessions for this renewal window. Can you advise if there's a path to preserve the relationship? If helpful, I'm available for a short call this afternoon.

Best,
Evan
Head of ML Platforms, Quantique Labs
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Evan Chu <evan.chu@quantique.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + ask for flexibility

Evan — thanks for the clear note and the attachment. I appreciate the context and urgency.

High level: we want to keep Quantique on platform. I can put together a targeted preserve offer but need approvals for any one-time credits and a deeper SLA commitment. Looping in Ben (deal lead) and Vivek (finance) to align on guardrails.

Proposed immediate next step: I’ll draft a mutual action plan with the commercial options (tiered discount + optional SLA top-up + one-time transition credit) and aim to share the formal offer by Monday EOD. Can you confirm whether procurement can sign a 12-month contract (they currently renew on a calendar year cadence) and whether there's flexibility on invoicing timing?

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + ask for flexibility

Received — good summary. My read: account is strategic enough to entertain a retention package but we need to limit precedent and protect blended unit economics. Initial parameters I'd support (subject to Rishi):

- One-time concession bucket: up to $40,000 credit (applied to first invoice)
- Year-1 list discount: 25% off current effective rate; Year-2 revert to standard pricing if multi-year
- SLA top-up: p95 inference latency guarantee during 9am–6pm PT for production route; failure triggers service credits (capped) not financial penalties beyond the credit bucket
- Term: lock for 12 months with a renewal review clause

I think this keeps the company whole and gives Quantique breathing room. Asking Rishi to weigh in on margin impact and any additional approvals we need from legal/governance.

—Ben
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + ask for flexibility

Ben/Laura — reviewed numbers and ran a quick sensitivity with finance. Approve the one-time $40k credit and a 25% first-year discount under these firm conditions:

1) Deal must be executed under deal_id DL-2026-2468 and booked in Q4 FY26 (to align with forecasting).
2) SLA credit structure: 5% of monthly invoice for each missed SLA event, capped at 30% of monthly invoice; total exposure limited to the $40k credit in year one.
3) Quantique must agree to a 12-month term and commit to a short performance review at month 9 with our CS team.
4) Any non-standard contract language (data residency, indemnity expansion) requires legal review and won't be part of the quick-sign package.

If legal needs to adjust wording, we do not release additional credit. With the above, I'm comfortable green-lighting. Vivek — if you can confirm booking cadence, we can finalize.

—Rishi
Chief Revenue Officer (acting), Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Evan Chu <evan.chu@quantique.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@quantique.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, procurement@quantique.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Quantique renewal offer (DL-2026-2468) — targeted preserve package

Evan / Samir — appreciate the quick sync earlier today. Per internal approvals, here is the formal preserve package we can offer to close the renewal by 2026-12-15: 

Offer summary:
- Contract term: 12 months (2027-01-15 to 2028-01-14)
- Year-1 effective discount: 25% off current effective rates
- One-time invoice credit: $40,000 applied to first invoice after signature
- SLA addendum: p95 inference latency guarantee during business hours (9am–6pm PT). SLA credits structured as 5% of monthly invoice per breach, capped at 30%/month and total exposure limited to the $40k credit in year one.
- Performance review with CS at month 9; renewal rate to be negotiated based on observed usage and performance.

Exclusions / notes:
- This package is contingent on execution of the standard MSA + SLA addendum (no custom indemnities or data residency clauses). Any legal redlines will require separate approval and may void the credit.
- Booking needs to be completed in Q4 FY26 (deal id DL-2026-2468).

Next steps:
1) If this is acceptable, I'll send a DocuSign link for the 12-month MSA + SLA addendum.
2) Procurement to confirm invoicing preference (Net 30 / Net 45).
3) Upon signature, credit will be applied to first invoice and CS will schedule the month-9 review.

Evan — we want to make this easy. Please let me know by EOD Wednesday if you can accept the package and preferred invoicing terms.

—Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: current_contract_excerpt.pdf
From: Evan Chu <evan.chu@quantique.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@quantique.com>, procurement@quantique.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quantique renewal offer (DL-2026-2468) — targeted preserve package

Laura — appreciate the fast turnaround and the clarity. The package looks workable. Two quick asks before we sign:

1) Procurement requests Net 45 invoicing for the first invoice only, then Net 30 thereafter.
2) We need a short clause in the SLA addendum that clarifies measurement methodology for the p95 (route definition + sampling window). Not a legal redline, more of an operational callout so we avoid ambiguity.

If those two items are fine, we'll route the DocuSign this afternoon. Thanks to you and the team for moving quickly.

—Evan
Head of ML Platforms, Quantique Labs
